summary: Missouri Conservation Commission tower near Fort Leonard Wood, built 1943 and replaced by a 100-foot tower in 1954-55; sold and removed from the site in February 2023.

facts.design: Steel tower: 85 ft (1943), replaced by a 100-foot steel tower in FY1954-55
facts.status_note: Sold and removed from the site in February 2023, per the Central US Lookouts page. The page does not say where the tower went or what remains on the site.

staffing.status: towerman James Krausland reported in 1944; James F. Crossland of Waynesville reported in 1947 and 1950

corrections.why: 25.9 m (85 ft) is the height of the 1943 tower only. The page says that tower was replaced by a 100-foot steel tower in FY1954-55, and that later tower is the last one the page describes before its 2023 removal.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: A 1948 newspaper item places the tower near Fort Leonard Wood on the margin of the Mark Twain National Forest; a 1949 newspaper item places it along U.S. Highway 66 near Waynesville. The story gives both.
A 1942 annual report lists 27 acres for the towersite; a 1943 report says seventy acres were acquired, and the 1945-46 manual gives 70 acres. The story reports the 1942 and 1943 figures.
The March 1944 Rolla Herald item spells the keeper's name Krausland; the 1947 and 1950 items spell it Crossland. The page does not say whether these are the same man.

notes_for_editor: The 2023 sale and removal rests on one line on this page. Two web searches for a Fort Wood or Fort Leonard Wood fire tower found nothing on it, and the Missouri Life article could not be read (HTTP 403). The 'Fort Wood' name and the Fort Leonard Wood name appear to refer to the same tower, but the page does not state that outright. The correction to height_m is an inference from the page's sequence: 1943 85 ft, 1954-55 replaced by a 100-foot tower; the page does not name the tower that was removed in 2023.
